description: Design a stack that supports push, pop, and an increment operation. increment(k, val) increments the bottom k elements by val. Implement CustomStack with a maximum size.
intuition: Instead of incrementing k elements every time (O(k)), store the increment lazily at position k-1. When popping, cascade the lazy increment down to the next element. This makes all three operations O(1).
approach: Use a lazy increment array. Instead of incrementing all k elements immediately, store the increment at index k-1. When popping, pass the increment down to the element below. This makes all operations O(1).
jsWalkthrough:
Input: CustomStack(3), push(1), push(2), pop(), push(2), push(3), push(4), increment(5,100), increment(2,100), pop(), pop(), pop(), pop()

push(1): stack=[1], inc=[0]
push(2): stack=[1,2], inc=[0,0]
pop(): idx=1, val=2+inc[1]=2, cascade inc[0]+=inc[1]=0, stack=[1], inc=[0] -> return 2
push(2): stack=[1,2], inc=[0,0]
push(3): stack=[1,2,3], inc=[0,0,0]
push(4): stack full (maxSize=3), ignore
increment(5,100): idx=min(5,3)-1=2, inc[2]+=100 -> inc=[0,0,100]
increment(2,100): idx=min(2,3)-1=1, inc[1]+=100 -> inc=[0,100,100]
pop(): idx=2, val=3+100=103, cascade inc[1]+=100 -> inc=[0,200,100], stack=[1,2] -> return 103
pop(): idx=1, val=2+200=202, cascade inc[0]+=200 -> inc=[200,200,100], stack=[1] -> return 202
pop(): idx=0, val=1+200=201, stack=[] -> return 201
pop(): stack empty -> return -1
explanation:
1. Maintain a stack and a parallel inc array for lazy increments.
2. push: add element and a 0 increment if not at max size.
3. increment(k, val): add val to inc[min(k, size) - 1]. This lazily marks the increment.
4. pop: return stack top + its increment. Pass the increment down to the element below.
5. All three operations run in O(1) time.
hints: Naive increment is O(k). Can you make it O(1)?
Use a lazy increment array that stores pending increments.
When popping, propagate the increment to the element below.
